swap.reason: The parts depend on things only she has — the jar wall, the koji cupboard, the ferment log, Brine, Sunday Pot, the ogiri pot — so another chef could not take it unchanged.

backdrop.reason: The agent's own fallback keeps every reveal intact without the 3D ("flat, still grid of the same jar photos, same tap-to-reveal labels"), so deleting it costs only decoration.

depth.reason: There is a deliberate arc — arrival, how the kitchen runs, the proof of the larder and the waste figure, people, roots, then a practical close — with placements the agent justifies by what precedes them.

clipart.reason: No object persists across the scroll; the WebGL jar is explicitly "used once" in the hero and then abandoned for unrelated CSS effects.

honesty.reason: The final plan uses September 2022, frames Fjaerland as a ten-week unpaid stage, says "we" with the one-month and bones caveats, and refuses to invent ferment-log values.

thirty_seconds.reason: The hero gives only her name and "Head Chef, Saltmarsh"; there is no navigation anywhere in the plan, so proof and contact sit at the bottom of a ten-section scroll.

plain_reader.reason: The opening is her name, her role and her own line "Most of what I care about happens before service" — plain to an outsider and credible to a cook.

judgement.summary: A ten-section scroll framed as walking through Ines's larder, built from her real material — jar wall, ferment log, koji cupboard, Brine, the ogiri pot — with careful rights handling, an honest rewrite of the waste figure and the stage, and thorough phone, reduced-motion and no-3D fallbacks. Its greatest weakness is structural: there is no object carried through the scroll and no form drawn from her own field (the ferment log it correctly identifies as how the kitchen runs is spent as one section rather than used as the page's shape), so the 3D is removable decoration over what is largely a renamed standard portfolio sequence with no navigation.
